3. It was alleged that the plaintiff was the rightful owner and possessor of above 58 decimal land and he transferred above land for a consideration of Taka 4,500 to the defendant by registered kobla deed dated 5-7-1987. In the same sitting and by the same scribe a deed of ekrarnama was written and executed by defendant No.1 stipulating the return of the disputed land to the plaintiff if within two years above consideration money was refunded. The plaintiff offered the return of above consideration money and return of possession of above land to the defendant but he refused. The plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.XII/12/87-88 to the Assistant Commissioner (land) under section 95ka of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. But the Assistant Commissioner rejected above case on the ground of non-registration of the ekrarnama. Against above order the plaintiff preferred an appeal to the Additional Deputy commissioner, Dinajpur which was dismissed. 

 15. It is proved by above legal evidence that defendant No.1 executed above Ekramama in the same sitting when registered kobla deed dated 15- 6-1987 was executed and above two documents together makes above transfer of the disputed land by the plaintiff to the defendant an usufractory mortgaged for 7 years as defined in section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 16. It is well settled that any agreement which was executed by the parties voluntarily and knowingly and which dose not contain any illegal terms can be enforced judicially. Since the deed of Ekramama Exhibit 1 is a legal document written and executed under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the same is legally enforceable by a competent Court of law.
